name: import_media
description: When: Bring files into the bin. Import local media files and block until each probe finishes (15s cap). Paths must be absolute (or file://). There is no directory-listing op: if the user named a file loosely ("GX010023.mp4 in Downloads", "the wedding clip"), glob or search with YOUR own filesystem tools, then pass the hits here. Returns {assets:[{id, index, name, kind, dur, pending}]}, plus missing:[paths that do not exist] and refreshed:[paths already in the bin] — treat a non-empty missing as "search again", not as a bin problem. A path already in the bin whose file changed on disk (same path, new content) is re-probed in place: its id is listed in reprobed and dur is the new length; clips keep the asset and are clamped if the media got shorter (undoable, "Media refreshed"). An id in stale could not be re-read and still describes the old file. On timeout returns error import_timeout with the same assets array and pending:true on the stragglers. Adding new files is not undoable.

folder.description: Bin folder id (or unique name) new files land in; "" for the bin root. Default: the folder the user is viewing. Paths already in the bin stay where they are

paths.description: Absolute file paths from your own filesystem search

previews.description: false: probe only; video and audio get no thumbnail or filmstrip until something needs one (the bin showing the file, or place_clip), which saves decoding on big scripted imports

name: list_assets
description: When: See what is in the bin. List imported assets. Returns {assets:[{index, id, name, kind, dur, w, h, folderId, proxy?}]}; proxy, on videos, is the create_proxies state; folderId "" is the bin root (see list_folders). usage:true adds clips, how many clips use each asset (inside composites too), and derived, how many assets were made from it (a stabilized render's original; in use even with clips 0; absent when none). There is no recording timestamp — "in the order I shot them" cannot be recovered from this list; sort by name or by the order they were imported.

name: remove_unused_assets
description: When: Clear media no clip uses. Remove every asset no clip uses (inside composites too), in one undo step. Kept: composite assets, each a whole nested timeline (kept_composites), and the originals of stabilized renders, which re-stabilizing reads (kept_sources); remove_asset takes one explicitly. dry_run:true only lists them. Returns {assets:[{id, name, kind}], removed, dry_run, kept_composites, kept_sources}. The files on disk are untouched.

dry_run.description: List what would go without removing it

name: list_missing_media
description: When: Find media whose file is gone. Returns {missing:[{asset, name, path, clips}], n}: assets whose file isn't there any more (moved, renamed, or on a drive this session can't see), with how many clips use each. Fix them with relink_media.

name: relink_media
description: When: Point moved media at its new place. Relinks missing media in one undo step. {from, to}: a folder or drive that moved, e.g. {from:"/mnt/hd/VIDEOS", to:"/mnt/x/VIDEOS"} (from may be another platform's path, e.g. "D:/footage"): each missing file under from is pointed at the same place under to (assets, clips, masks, transcripts, effect files). {search_dir}: finds each missing asset's file by name under that folder; missing files of one name it can't tell apart (no known size, or the same one) aren't guessed, and a search cut short at 200,000 files relinks nothing. A file is only relinked when it's there, isn't another asset's, and is the same size as before (when known); files still in place aren't touched. Returns {relinked:[{from, to}], n (paths), matched (from/to only: paths under from), still_missing:[{path, reason, tried?, asset?, candidates?}], still_missing_n, truncated?}; lists cut at 200. Error locked when a locked track holds one of the clips (a dry_run can't foresee that). dry_run:true reports without changing anything.

search_dir.description: Folder to search for missing files by name

name: create_proxies
description: When: Make preview proxies for footage. Queue preview proxies (small, fast-decoding copies preview reads instead of the original; export always reads the original). Pick assets, the assets of clips, all:true (every video in the bin) or all_slow:true (every video that would preview slowly: past 1080p, or 10-bit HEVC/AV1/VP9; probes each file, error timeout past a minute). A composite isn't a video: pick the clips inside it. Built one at a time in the background: poll proxy_status. Preview only reads them with useProxies on (set_ui_preferences). Not undoable: a proxy is a cache. Returns {queued:[ids], already:[{asset, state}], skipped:[{asset|clip, reason: not_video|missing|no_media|gone}], not_slow? (all_slow), queue:{busy, progress, current, queued}, useProxies, proxySize, proxyLocation, proxyFolder}.

all_slow.description: Every video asset that would preview slowly

items.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

clips.description: Clip ids whose assets get proxies

name: proxy_status
description: When: Check preview proxies. Per-asset proxy state for video assets: none, queued, building, ready (made by Drift at the current size) or linked (a file made elsewhere, matched by name). A failed build reads none with error. Default every video asset; or pick assets/clips. Returns {proxies:[{asset, name, state, error?, location?, path?}], counts:{state: n}, truncated? (rows cut at 500), queue:{busy, progress, current, queued}, useProxies, proxySize, proxyLocation, proxyFolder}; picked assets or clips with no video come back in skipped. location (ready/linked rows): beside, folder, cache or linked.

items.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

name: remove_proxies
description: When: Delete preview proxies. Drop queued proxies, stop one being built and delete the proxies Drift made at the current size (assets, clips or all:true). A linked proxy (made elsewhere) is never deleted. Not undoable. Returns {removed:[ids], kept:[{asset|clip, reason: none|linked|not_video|no_media}], queue, useProxies, proxySize, proxyLocation, proxyFolder}.

items.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

clips.description: Clip ids whose assets lose their proxies

name: cancel_proxies
description: When: Stop building proxies. Empty the proxy queue (automatic ones from import included) and stop the one being built; one whose last frames already landed may still finish. Proxies already made stay. Returns {cancelled, queue, useProxies, proxySize, proxyLocation, proxyFolder}.

name: rename_asset
description: When: Rename a bin row. Rename an asset in the bin. Does not rename the file on disk. On a composite asset it renames that timeline, tab included.

asset.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

name: list_folders
description: When: See the bin's folder tree. List media-bin folders. Returns {folders:[{id, name, parentId, count}]}; parentId "" is the bin root and count is the number of assets directly inside.

name: create_folder
description: When: Make a bin folder. Create a media-bin folder. Names need not be unique. Returns {id}.

parent.description: Parent folder id (or unique name); omit or "" for the bin root

name: move_asset_to_folder
description: When: File an asset into a bin folder. Move a bin asset into a folder. Clips on the timeline are unaffected. Returns {asset, folderId, changed}.

asset.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

folder.description: Folder id (or unique name); "" for the bin root

name: rename_folder
description: When: Rename a bin folder. Rename a media-bin folder. Returns {id, name, changed}.

name: delete_folder
description: When: Remove a bin folder. Delete a media-bin folder. By default its assets and subfolders move up to its parent, as in the app. recursive:true instead removes every subfolder and every asset under it from the bin; it fails in_use (changing nothing) if any of those assets has clips on the timeline, and locked if one of them is a timeline with a locked track. One undo step. Returns {deleted:[folder ids], removedAssets}.

recursive.description: Also remove subfolders and their assets (default false)

name: remove_asset
description: When: Delete a bin row. Remove an asset from the media bin. Refused with in_use while any clip uses it, on any timeline; list_assets({usage:true}) counts them. A composite asset is a whole timeline: removing it deletes that timeline and everything in it and closes its tab (editing falls back to the main timeline); refused with locked when that timeline has a locked track. One undo step.

asset.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

name: replace_asset
description: When: Swap source file. Point an existing bin row at a different file. Every clip using the asset switches to the new media, keeping its trim and timeline position — trims past the new file's duration are clamped downstream. The file is always re-read, also when it is the same path with new content; the call waits for that (15s cap) and returns the asset as now probed (dur, kind) with reprobed:[id], or replace_failed; past the cap import_timeout, with pending:true to poll.

asset.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

path.description: Absolute path or file:// URL; must exist

name: refresh_asset
description: When: Re-read a file changed on disk. Re-probe an asset's own file after it was rewritten at the same path, and drop every cached decode, thumbnail, waveform and preview proxy of the old content. Keeps the asset's name, bin trim and rotation; clips keep the asset and are clamped if the media got shorter. Blocks until the probe lands (15s cap). import_media of the same path does this on its own when the file's size or modification time changed; use this when they did not (e.g. a copy that preserved mtime). Returns {assets:[{id, index, name, kind, dur, pending}], stale} — stale:true means the file could not be re-read (or is now another kind of media) and the asset still describes the old file.

asset.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

name: export_asset_image
description: When: Export a still from an asset. Write an image file from a bin asset (its poster frame for video). Creates parent folders. The format follows the path's extension.

asset.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

path.description: Absolute output path, extension picks the format

name: import_media_bytes
description: When: Import from base64. Decode base64 bytes to a file, then import it like import_media. ALWAYS pass an explicit `path`: with only `name` the file is written to a temporary directory that is deleted as soon as the call returns, leaving the asset pointing at a missing file. Returns the same shape as import_media.

name.description: Filename hint (e.g. clip.mp4). Used only when path is omitted.

path.description: Absolute write path — strongly recommended; parent folders are created

name: inspect_pdf
description: When: Page count of a PDF, and whether the viewer addon is installed. Read-only. Give path for a file, or clip for a PDF clip already on the timeline (adds its options: firstPage, lastPage, layout, gridColumns, gap, scrollX, scrollY, zoom, keyframes). Returns pageCount (0 when the pdfium addon is missing), addonAvailable and addonId; install_addon with that id when it is missing.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: set_pdf_options
description: When: Pages shown and layout of a PDF clip. Choose which pages a PDF clip shows and how they are laid out; only supplied keys change. Pages are 1-based and clamp to the document once its page count is known. Scrolling and zoom are not set here: keyframe pdf.scrollX, pdf.scrollY (page units) and pdf.zoom (0.1..10) with set_keyframe.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

gap.description: Space between pages in PDF points (default 12)

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

lastPage.description: Last page shown; 0 = through the last page

layout.description: Pages stacked in a column, side by side in a row, or in a grid

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: set_asset_rotation
description: When: Fix a sideways video in the bin. Override the bin asset's orientation losslessly (the decoder rotates; nothing is re-encoded). degrees is absolute 0/90/180/270; -1 returns to the file's own rotation tag. Clips already on the timeline keep their own correction — use set_clip_orientation for those. Returns {asset, degrees, changed}.

asset.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

name: add_track
description: When: Need a new lane. Prepend a track. New track becomes index 0, so every existing track index shifts down by one — re-read inspect before reusing track/index clip references. type transform adds a transform layer: a parent transform over every visual track from just below it down to span_end (default: the lowest visual track), holding one identity clip over the whole timeline. Returns {track, clip, span:{end, covers}} for it; move the group with set_transform on that clip.

span_end.description: transform only: index (as numbered before the add) of the last track the layer covers

name: make_transform_layer
description: When: Move several tracks as one. Add a transform layer directly above the topmost track holding one of `clips`, covering down to the lowest, with one clip over their time range (or [at, at+dur)). The clips keep their own transforms; set_transform on the returned clip moves, scales, rotates, turns in 3D (layer3d) and fades the whole group. One undo step. Returns {clip, track, index, span:{end, covers}}.

at.description: Start in seconds (default: the clips' earliest start)

dur.description: Duration in seconds (default: to the clips' latest end)

name: add_camera
description: When: Add the scene camera, or cut to a new framing. One viewpoint the whole timeline is seen through: position, rotation, an optional point of interest and zoom, all animatable. Adds the camera lane if it is missing. Without `at` the clip covers the whole sequence (what a first camera wants); with `at` it is one clip starting there, so two in a row read as a camera cut. A camera at rest looks exactly like no camera, so adding one changes nothing until you move it. Frame it with set_keyframe on the returned clip (for a path of several keys, write them with set_keyframes and interpolation "smooth" in one call) using positionX/positionY/z (the eye, world px: canvas top-left origin, y down, +z away from the viewer; at rest [w/2, h/2, -zoom]), rotationX/rotationY/rotation (pitch, yaw, roll, degrees; yaw is applied first, so the horizon stays level with zero roll), anchorX/anchorY/anchorZ (the point of interest, used when camera_look_at is given aimAtTarget:true) and perspective (zoom, px; real zoom, the eye does not move). With no keys, set_transform moves it too. While a camera runs it replaces each clip's own perspective, because a scene has one viewer. Returns {clip, track, index}.

at.description: Start in seconds (default: the whole sequence)

name: set_transform_span
description: When: Change which tracks a transform layer covers. Set the last track the transform layer at `track` covers, by track index (`end`) or by a clip on it (`end_clip`). The end must be a visual track below the layer and may not cut through a nested layer's span or reach past an enclosing one; bad_args lists the valid ends. Returns {track, span:{end, covers}}.

end.description: Index of the last covered track

end_clip.description: A clip id on the last covered track

track.description: Transform layer track index

name: remove_track
description: When: Delete a lane and its clips. Delete a track and everything on it.

track.description: Track index

name: set_track
description: When: Mute, solo, hide, lock or keep a lane out of export. Set track muted/hidden/locked/solo. solo:true makes only soloed tracks heard (mute and hide still apply to a soloed track), in every timeline mix: playback, get_waveform, loudness and range measurements, export_video; solo:false clears it. The picture is unaffected, it is saved with the project, and inspect marks the track solo:true. Only an audio or video track can be soloed; solo:false works on any track. exclude_from_export:true makes it a review track: still shown and heard while editing, but left out of export_video and flatten_composite (e.g. a subtitle lane with the VO script to read along); export_video doesn't reuse a bake where its clips show (the preview still plays it). Refused on a transform or camera layer. Undoable.

exclude_from_export.description: Keep this track out of export (a review track)

solo.description: Hear only soloed tracks (audio; the picture is unaffected)

track.description: Track index

name: place_clip
description: When: Put media on the timeline. Place an asset as a clip and return the new clip's id. When overlap is off (default) the start is pushed to the next free gap; the reply carries requested, placed, and reason:"gap" when they differ. Note `track` means two different things: with new_track:true it is the insert position of the new track, otherwise it is the destination track and a type mismatch fails type_mismatch. With `track` omitted, the first track accepting this asset is used, and a new track is created if none does. A composite asset (a timeline) goes on the main timeline only, and only once it has content.

asset.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

new_track.description: Insert a new matching track above

track.description: Destination track, or insert position when new_track is true

name: insert_clip
description: When: Insert media and push the rest along. Insert an asset as a clip at an exact point, in one undo step. The point is `at` (seconds), or `before`/`after` a clip id. With ripple (default true) every later clip on the track moves right by the new clip's length, and so does every later clip on the tracks holding their linked audio, so A/V stays in sync; effect adjustments follow their clips. A locked track it would change refuses the insert. With ripple the point must be at a clip boundary or in a gap, not inside a clip (split it first); without it the space must already be free. `in`/`out` are source seconds within the media (default: the asset's bin trim, else its whole length); a range past the media fails bad_args. `track` defaults to the track of `before`/`after`, else the first that accepts the asset. Returns the new clip {id, track, index, start, dur, in, out}, moved:[{id, start}] with the final start of every clip the ripple moved, and removed_transitions:[ids] when a transition at the cut had to go (its clips no longer touch).

after.description: Clip id to insert after (its end)

asset.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

before.description: Clip id to insert before (its start)

in.description: Source in, seconds (default: the bin trim's in, else 0)

out.description: Source out, seconds (default: the bin trim's out, else the media's end)

ripple.description: Push later clips right to make room

track.description: Destination track

name: move_clip
description: When: Change a clip's start time. Move a clip on its track. When overlap is off (default) the start may be pushed forward to the next gap; the reply carries requested, placed, and reason:"gap" when they differ. Or reorder: before/after (a clip id on the same track) puts it at that clip's start or end and moves the clips in between by its length, linked tracks too, in one undo step; the reply adds moved:[{id, start}] and any removed_transitions. Refused when the two are linked, a track is locked, or a clip would land on another or before 0.

before.description: Clip id to move in front of

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: set_sequence
description: When: Lay a track out from a list. Make `track` exactly `clips`, end to end from `start` (default 0), in one undo step. An entry is {clip} (a clip on this track, keeping its settings) or {asset}, each with optional in/out (source seconds) and name. Unlisted clips on the track are deleted with their linked audio and effects; listed clips' linked audio moves with them. Refused, nothing changed, for a clip from another track or listed twice, a range past the media, clips linked to each other, a locked or adjustment track, or linked audio landing on another clip or before 0. Clear a track with delete_clips. Returns clips:[{id, start, dur}] in order, created, removed and any removed_transitions.

asset.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

clip.description: Clip id on this track

start.description: Where the first clip starts, seconds

track.description: Track index

name: replace_clip
description: When: Put new media under a clip. Swap the clip's media for another asset in place, in one undo step. The clip keeps its name, transform, effects and keyframes; linked audio follows when the new file has sound. A silent file leaves linked audio in place, loosely linked. in/out set the new source range (neither: the clip's length, shorter if the file runs out; a still takes none). With ripple (default) later clips, linked tracks too, move by the change in length; without, a longer clip must not land on the next. Returns moved:[{id, start}] and any removed_transitions.

asset.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

in.description: Source in, seconds (alone: to the media's end)

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

ripple.description: Move later clips by the change in length

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: swap_clips
description: When: Exchange two clips' places. Swap two clips on one track in one undo step: each takes the other's place, the clips between them move by the difference in length, and linked A/V moves along. Refused for different tracks, linked clips, a locked track, or a clip landing on another or before 0. Returns moved:[{id, start}] and any removed_transitions.

name: set_duration
description: When: Change timeline length. Set the clip's timeline duration in seconds. Trims source out (or in if reversed). Clamped to the source material left after the current trim, so the applied dur in the reply may be shorter than requested; clips with no intrinsic length (text, shape, still image) accept any duration.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: set_trim
description: When: Set source in/out. Set source in/out points in seconds. Recomputes timeline duration from the span and speed. Values are not validated here — out <= in or a span past the end of the source is clamped downstream; read back in/out/dur from the reply. ripple:true (default false) also trims the clip's linked audio the same way and moves every later clip on its track (and on the tracks of their linked audio) by the change in length, whatever set_ripple says, in the same undo step; the reply then adds moved:[{id, start}]. A locked track it would change refuses it, and so does a clip sitting in the space a shorter trim would close.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

ripple.description: Later clips follow the new length

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: slip_clip
description: When: Show another part of the media in the same slot. Slip: move the clip's source window and keep its start and length. by: source seconds (+ = later in the media, at any speed or direction), or in: the new source in point. Linked audio slips with it; a loosely linked clip doesn't. Stops at the media's ends: the reply has requested (echoes by, or the in point), slipped (the applied move, a delta in source seconds), and reason:"media_start"|"media_end" when it stopped short. A looped clip shifts its repeat instead, with no limit (by only; the reply adds loop_offset). Keyframes, fades, effects and transitions stay on the timeline. Face, depth, tracker and matte data follow the source but only cover the range they were analysed on (source_data lists them), and keys baked from them stay (baked_keys). Generated captions follow their words; cues whose words slip out are removed, and a caption clip left empty goes too (retimed_subtitles). One undo step. Refused for clips with no media (titles, shapes, stills, adjustments) and on a locked track, including a locked caption track or a locked lane holding a pinned effect of a removed caption clip (the whole slip is refused).

by.description: Source seconds to move the window; + is later in the media

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: move_to_track
description: When: Move a clip to another lane. Move a clip to another track. Type must match the destination, else type_mismatch.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: split_clip
description: When: Cut a clip in two. Split a clip at `at` seconds (default: playhead). `at` must fall strictly inside the clip, else bad_args. Returns {clips:[original id, new id], at}; the original id keeps the left part.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: delete_clip
description: When: Remove a clip. Delete a clip and its linked A/V partner. Reversible with undo. The clip's effects and masks live on adjustments pinned to it; by default they stay on the timeline, unlinked, and keep applying to whatever sits under them. with_effects:true deletes them too, in the same undo step.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

with_effects.description: Also delete the adjustments pinned to the clip (its effects and masks). Default false

name: delete_clips
description: When: Remove several clips and close up. Delete several clips in one undo step, with their linked A/V partners. With ripple (default true) the space they leave is closed, whatever set_ripple says: later clips move left, together with every track joined to theirs by linked clips, so A/V stays in sync. Overlapping or adjacent spaces close as one. A clip in the way on one of those tracks, or a locked one, refuses the delete (nothing changes). with_effects (default true, unlike delete_clip) also deletes the adjustments pinned to them. All ids must exist, or nothing is deleted (not_found lists the unknown ones). Returns removed:[ids] (partners and effects included) and moved:[{id, start}] with the final start of every clip that moved.

with_effects.description: Also delete the adjustments pinned to them

name: duplicate_clip
description: When: Copy a clip after itself. Duplicate a clip immediately after it on the same track. Returns the new clip's id.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: undo
description: When: Revert the last edit. Undo the last project edit; one apply batch is one step. Fails bad_args when the stack is empty. Does not cover the ops in catalog.limitations (import, save, playback, export, view-state toggles). set_beat_layers is the dangerous one: it changes the user's own snapping and cannot be undone. Use list_history and undo_to to jump further back.

name: redo
description: When: Re-apply an undone edit. Redo the last undone edit. Fails bad_args when there is nothing to redo.

name: list_history
description: When: Read the undo stack. Linear history (no branches). Returns {entries:[{index, label, short, snapshot?}] newest first, current, hash, short, total, linear:true}. index 0 is Origin (empty/loaded project); each later entry is one undo step. short is the first 12 chars of that version's SHA-256 (undo_to takes any ≥8-char prefix); hash is the full HEAD hash — the same bytes take_snapshot writes to <hash>.json. With an undo step limit set, each new step can drop the oldest and renumber the rest: keep the hash, not the index, across edits. Read-only.

name: undo_to
description: When: Jump to a history version. Restore the project to a linear history version. Pass index (from list_history) or hash (full SHA-256 or unique 8+ char prefix). Redo of later steps remains until the next edit, which discards them — there is no branching. Not itself undoable.

hash.description: Content hash from list_history, or a unique prefix

index.description: Target index from list_history (0 = Origin)

name: take_snapshot
description: When: Keep a JSON copy of HEAD. Write the current history version as compact project JSON named <hash>.json under the app history folder. The file's SHA-256 is the same hash list_history reports. Does not change the project. Caps at 32 files (oldest dropped). Not undoable.

label.description: Optional note stored only in the reply

name: clear_history
description: When: Free undo history. Drop undo history to free memory and shrink the next save: keeps the newest keep_last steps that can be undone (default 0: none) and drops every undone (redo) step. The project is unchanged; media only the dropped steps used is no longer kept for them. Returns {removed, steps, index}. Not undoable.

name: set_history_limit
description: When: Cap or stop undo history. This project's own undo history setting, saved with it; each part set overrides the app setting the user picks in Settings › General. steps: most steps that can be undone, oldest dropped first; 0 = no history, -1 = no limit; a non-zero value turns history on even when the app has it off. persist: true saves history into the project, false keeps it for this session only (with history on again, unset persist follows the app setting, or the session when the app has history off). reset:true drops both parts first. Returns {mode, steps, source, steps_kept}. Not undoable.

persist.description: Save history into the project (true) or keep it for this session only (false)

reset.description: Drop this project's setting and use the app's

steps.description: Most undoable steps; 0 = no history, -1 = no limit

name: history_stats
description: When: How much undo history holds. Returns {steps, undoable, redoable, snapshots (project copies held in memory), saved_with_project, history_only_media (count of files only history still uses), history_only_media_paths (first 20), settings:{mode, steps, source}}. size:true adds json_bytes, the history as uncompressed JSON (what a save adds before compression; memory use is higher and not measured); it serialises every state, so it is slow on a long history.

name: list_snapshots
description: When: On-disk history JSON files. Snapshots written by take_snapshot. Returns {snapshots:[{hash, short, path, bytes, savedAt}]}.

name: restore_snapshot
description: When: Reset to a saved JSON. If hash is still on the undo stack, same as undo_to. Otherwise load the on-disk JSON and clear the stack (new Origin). Linear — redo history is discarded. Not undoable.

name: changes
description: When: What changed since a revision. The edits after revision `since` (from inspect or a previous call), oldest first, made in the editor or by you, undo/redo included. Each: {revision, source:mcp|ui, kind:edit|undo|redo, label, clips:[{id, change:added|removed|changed, track, sequence, fields, from_track, split_from}], tracks, assets, settings}; a batch is one entry. Without since, just the current revision. more:true: call again from the last revision. The log starts at your first call this session and keeps 500 edits; truncated:true (or detail:false on an old entry) means some detail is gone: re-read inspect.

name: diff
description: When: Compare two project versions. What differs between two states: clips added, removed or changed (with the fields), tracks and assets. from/to: a hash from list_history or take_snapshot (8+ chars) or "head" (default for to). E.g. check a scripted round, or what undo_to would revert.

name: set_overlap
description: When: Allow clips to overlap. Project setting. Off (default): place/move push to the next gap. On: requested start is kept.

name: move_track
description: When: Change which lane sits above which. Move a track from one index to another; the tracks between them shift. Every track index and every track+index clip reference you hold is invalidated — re-read inspect after this.

name: set_track_waveform
description: When: Toggle the waveform drawing on a lane (cosmetic). Toggle waveform display on an audio/video track row. Cosmetic — does not affect rendering or export.

track.description: Track index

name: set_track_height
description: When: Resize a lane. Set the track's row height multiplier, 0.6..4.0. Cosmetic — does not affect rendering or export.

track.description: Track index

name: select_clip
description: When: Focus one clip. Select exactly one clip, replacing any previous selection. REQUIRED before the selection-based ops, which take no clip argument: separate_audio, unlink_audio, link_clips, merge_clips, align_clip_left, align_clip_right, copy_selection, cut_selection. freeze_frame and paste_at_playhead are playhead-based — seek first, do not select.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: clear_selection
description: When: Deselect every clip so selection-based ops stop applying. Clear the clip selection. Selection-based ops fail afterwards until you select again.

name: select_all_clips
description: When: Select every clip before copy_selection or cut_selection. Select every clip on the timeline. Useful before copy_selection or cut_selection.

name: copy_selection
description: When: Copy to clipboard. Copy the selected clips to the internal clipboard. Acts on the current selection — call select_clip or select_all_clips first. Paste with paste_at_playhead.

name: cut_selection
description: When: Cut to clipboard. Cut the selected clips to the internal clipboard, removing them from the timeline. Acts on the current selection — call select_clip or select_all_clips first.

name: paste_at_playhead
description: When: Drop the copied/cut clips at the playhead. Paste the internal clipboard at the playhead. Requires an earlier copy_selection or cut_selection; returns ok with no effect when the clipboard is empty. Playhead-based — seek first; selecting a clip does not change where this lands. Returns {ids:[…], n} of the new clips.

name: separate_audio
description: When: Pull a video clip's audio onto its own lane. Detach the audio of the selected video clip onto its own audio track. Acts on the current selection — call select_clip first; fails bad_args when nothing separable is selected.

name: unlink_audio
description: When: Break A/V link. Break the link between paired audio/video clips in the selection so they can be moved and trimmed independently. Acts on the current selection — call select_clip first; fails bad_args when no linked clips are selected.

name: link_clips
description: When: Pair clips so they move and trim together. Link two or more selected, currently unlinked clips (typically a video and an audio from different media) so they select, move, split and delete together, and trimming one moves the others' matching edge by the same amount, while each keeps its own duration and speed. Acts on the current selection — call select_clips first; fails bad_args when fewer than two unlinked clips are selected.

name: make_composite
description: When: Collapse clips into one composite clip. Move the selected clips (with their linked audio and pinned adjustments) into a new nested timeline and put one composite clip in their place, plus a composite item in the bin. Acts on the current selection — call select_clips first. Only on the main timeline (one level of nesting: not inside a composite or a new_timeline timeline), and the selection must not already contain a composite. Returns {clip, sequence, asset}.

name: dissolve_composite
description: When: Turn a composite back into its clips. Release the selected composite clip's inner clips onto the main timeline at their original times, cut to the composite's trim, and remove the composite. The composite's own effects, transform, fades and keyframes are discarded. Fails when the composite is ramped, reversed or not at 1x, and with locked when a locked track would be changed or deleted (a main-timeline track the clips land on, or the composite's own timeline when this is its last instance). Acts on the current selection — call select_clip first.

name: open_composite
description: When: Edit inside a composite. Open a composite's timeline in its own tab and make it the timeline every other op edits (tracks, clips, inspect). Composites are the project's other timelines: the ones make_composite collapses clips into and the ones new_timeline starts. Name it by a composite clip (clip or track+index), by sequence id, or pass main:true to return to the main timeline; close_timeline closes a tab. Export always renders the main timeline. Not an undo step.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

main.description: Switch back to the main timeline

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: list_composites
description: When: Composites, their tabs and which is open. List every composite, which means every timeline besides the main one (from make_composite or new_timeline, empty ones included): {sequence, asset, name, duration, open, active}. open: its tab is open; active marks the timeline being edited; activeSequence is empty on the main timeline. rename_asset({asset, name}) renames one; remove_asset deletes one no clip uses.

name: new_timeline
description: When: Start an empty timeline (a Short, alt cut). Create an empty timeline, as Assets panel → New timeline does: a composite with one video track at the project's canvas size and fps, plus its composite item in the bin. name defaults to the first free "Timeline N"; names need not be unique, and rename_asset renames it later. open (default true) opens its tab and makes it the timeline every other op edits (tracks, clips, inspect), as open_composite does; open:false leaves the edited timeline as it was. One undo step; redo recreates it without reopening it. It uses the project's canvas, fps and export settings, and export_video still renders only the main timeline. Returns {sequence, asset, name, activeSequence}.

folder.description: Bin folder id (or unique name) for its bin item; "" for the bin root. Default: the folder the user is viewing

name.description: Timeline name (default: the first free "Timeline N")

open.description: Open its tab and edit it (default true)

name: close_timeline
description: When: Close a timeline's tab. Close a composite timeline's tab (sequence from list_composites or new_timeline). When it is the timeline being edited, every op goes back to the main timeline. The timeline, its clips and its bin item stay; open_composite({sequence}) reopens it. The main timeline has no tab. A sequence whose tab isn't open is a no-op (closed:false). Not an undo step, and never makes the project unsaved on its own. Returns {closed, activeSequence}.

name: flatten_composite
description: When: Render a composite clip to a video file. Render the composite clip's range to a new video file, add it to the bin and swap the clip (and audio separated from it) over to it. Async: returns {started:true}; poll export_status. Transparency around the composite's content becomes the project background.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: merge_clips
description: When: Join adjacent clips, or several subtitle clips into one. Merge the selected adjacent clips on one track back into a single clip. Acts on the current selection — select the clips first; fails bad_args when the selection cannot be merged. Two or more subtitle clips on one track (select_clips) always merge, gaps allowed: the result spans first start to last end, holds every cue, and keeps the earliest clip's style and transform. Pass track instead to merge every subtitle clip on that track, ignoring the selection.

track.description: Merge every subtitle clip on this track

name: align_clip_left
description: When: Snap start to zero. Move the selected clip so it starts at 0. Acts on the current selection — call select_clip first.

name: align_clip_right
description: When: Snap end to duration. Move the selected clip so it ends at the project duration. Acts on the current selection — call select_clip first.

name: set_clip_name
description: When: Rename a clip. Set the clip's display name on the timeline. Cosmetic; does not touch the bin asset.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: set_clip_label
description: When: Tag a clip with a stable label. Set the clip's label (empty clears it): a tag that survives renames, shown in the inspector. A split or duplicate gives the copy the next number (intro, intro.2, intro.3); the original keeps its label. Find clips by it with find_clips.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: find_clips
description: When: Search clips by label or name. Clips matching every filter given: label (exact; an unnumbered label also finds its numbered copies; "" finds unlabelled clips), name (case-insensitive substring), asset, track, kind. Returns clips:[{id, track, label, name, kind, start, duration, ...}] in timeline order.

asset.description: Asset id, bin index (number or numeric string), or exact asset name (case-insensitive). A numeric value is tried as a bin index first, so prefer the id from list_assets.

kind.description: Clip kind, e.g. video, audio, text

track.description: Track index

name: add_bookmark
description: When: Mark a time. Add a bookmark at `at` seconds. Does not return its index — bookmarks are addressed by position in inspect({detail:true}).bookmarks, so re-read that before removing or updating.

name: remove_bookmark
description: When: Remove a marker by its position in the bookmark list. Remove a bookmark by its position in inspect({detail:true}).bookmarks. Later bookmarks shift down one index.

index.description: 0-based position in inspect({detail:true}).bookmarks — bookmarks have no stable id, so re-read that list before using this and after any bookmark is removed.

name: update_bookmark
description: When: Move or relabel an existing marker. Update a bookmark's time and/or label. Pass BOTH at and label: an omitted field is read back from the existing bookmark, and an out-of-range index is not checked on that path. Verify the index against inspect({detail:true}).bookmarks first.

at.description: Seconds; omitted keeps the current time

index.description: 0-based position in inspect({detail:true}).bookmarks — bookmarks have no stable id, so re-read that list before using this and after any bookmark is removed.

label.description: Label; omitted keeps the current label

name: go_to_bookmark
description: When: Seek to bookmark. Move the playhead to a bookmark, addressed by its position in inspect({detail:true}).bookmarks.

index.description: 0-based position in inspect({detail:true}).bookmarks — bookmarks have no stable id, so re-read that list before using this and after any bookmark is removed.

name: freeze_frame
description: When: Hold current frame. Insert a still of the frame under the playhead as a new clip. Uses the playhead, not a clip argument and not the selection — seek first. Returns {id, track, index} of the new still.

name: get_camera_state
description: When: Read the scene camera's pose at a time. The camera clip covering `at` (default the playhead), or `clip`, as it is posed then, keyframes included. Returns {active, at, clip, track, x, y, z, rotationX, rotationY, rotation, aimAtTarget, poi:[x,y,z], zoom, focalLength, fov, eye:[x,y,z]}; active:false when no camera covers that time. Units: x/y/z (and eye) are the camera's position in the 3D world: canvas px from the top-left, y down, +z away from the viewer, so a camera at rest has eye [w/2, h/2, -zoom]. rotationX/Y/rotation are pitch/yaw/roll in degrees, right-handed in that world and applied yaw first (+rotationX looks up, +rotationY looks toward +x, +rotation rolls clockwise on screen); the horizon stays level when roll is 0. With aimAtTarget the camera faces poi (a world point, level horizon) and the rotation is an extra offset in the camera's own frame. zoom is the distance in px at which the canvas fills the frame; focalLength is the same value in mm on a 36 x 24 mm film back and fov the vertical field of view in degrees (set zoom, i.e. perspective, to change any of them). Read-only.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: reset_camera
description: When: Return the scene camera to rest. Clears the camera clip's position, rotation and point of interest, keyframes included, and switches aimAtTarget off, and clears the zoom (perspective) back to its default, so it looks exactly like no camera. One undo step. `clip` defaults to the camera covering the playhead; not_found when there is no camera (add_camera).

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: camera_look_at
description: When: Aim the scene camera at a clip or point. Turns the camera in place (its eye stays put) so `target` lands at the canvas centre with a level horizon: rotationX/rotationY are set and the roll is reset to 0; zoom is kept. With aimAtTarget:true the camera instead stays locked on the target (a two-node camera): the point of interest is written (anchorX/Y/Z) and the rotation offset cleared; aimAtTarget:false switches that off again. target is a clip id (its centre in the 3D world, including z; transform-layer parents are ignored) or a world point {x,y,z} in canvas px from the top-left (y down, +z away from the viewer; z defaults to 0). `at` (default the playhead) is where the aim is computed and, with keyframe:true, where keys are written; a property that is already animated always takes a key, otherwise the plain value is written (like set_transform). One undo step. Returns the new pose and eye. Needs a camera: add_camera first. For a path over several keys, write the eye with set_keyframes and interpolation "smooth".

aimAtTarget.description: true = lock on the target via the point of interest; false = free rotation (default: unchanged)

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

keyframe.description: Write keyframes at `at` instead of plain values

target.description: Clip id to look at, or a world point {x,y,z} in canvas px from the canvas top-left (+z away)

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: camera_move
description: When: Animate a classic camera move. Writes a start and an end keyframe on the camera props the move changes, from the pose at `start`; one undo step. Moves and `amount` (default): dolly_in/dolly_out along the view direction (px, 300); truck_left/truck_right sideways (px, 200); crane_up/crane_down (px, 200); pan_left/pan_right and tilt_up/tilt_down turn the camera in place (degrees, 20 and 15); orbit_left/orbit_right circle `target` about the vertical axis while keeping it centred (degrees, 45; target is a clip id or {x,y,z} world point, default the canvas centre); push_in/pull_out zoom the lens in or out (zoom x(1+amount) or x(1-amount), a fraction 0..0.9, default 0.35) without moving the eye; use dolly to move closer. Orbit keys interpolate pose linearly, so an orbit past ~90 degrees is a chord rather than an arc; split it. easing is ease (default) or linear. start..end must lie inside the camera clip (default: the one covering `start`). Needs add_camera first.

amount.description: Size: px, degrees or lens fraction depending on the move

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

target.description: Orbit centre: clip id or {x,y,z} world point (default the canvas centre)

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: set_ripple
description: When: Ripple delete and trim. Project setting. When on, deleting or shortening a clip pulls later clips on that track left to close the hole. Off (default): every delete leaves a gap. Not undoable.

name: close_gap
description: When: Close one hole on a track. Shift every clip on `track` that starts at or after `at` left by the width of the gap whose left edge is `at` (typically the end of the preceding clip, or 0 for the hole before the first clip, which moves the track to the start of the timeline). Linked A/V partners follow. With overlap off this is how you delete without leaving a hole, or how you put an intro at the front: place then close_gap behind. When moving several clips toward zero with overlap off, sequence back-to-front or each move is pushed into the clip ahead. With all_tracks:true, every track that is empty over the gap closes it too, so unlinked audio, titles and layers keep their timing. A track with a clip in the gap stays (with the tracks linked to it), as does a locked track. The reply lists moved_tracks, skipped_tracks:[{track, reason: clip_in_gap|locked|linked, blocker}] and moved:[{id, start}]. Refused (nothing changes) when this track's own group cannot close, or when it is an adjustment track. `at` within a millisecond of a clip's end counts as that end.

all_tracks.description: Also close the gap on every other track that is empty over it

at.description: Left edge of the hole, timeline seconds

track.description: Track index

name: close_gaps
description: When: Close every hole on a track. Close every gap on `track` within [from, to] (seconds; default the whole track) in one undo step: the hole before the first clip and each hole between clips, latest first. Later clips move left, together with every track joined to this one by linked clips, so A/V stays in sync. A gap that a clip on such a track sits in (or whose close would drag an earlier linked clip along, or past 0) is left open and listed in skipped with that clip; a locked track or an adjustment track refuses the op. Returns closed:[{at, width}] and skipped:[{at, width, blocker}] at their positions before the op, and moved:[{id, start}]. all_tracks:true closes each gap on every track that is empty over it as well; moved_tracks and skipped_tracks:[{track, at, reason, blocker}] are added to the reply.

all_tracks.description: Also close each gap on every other track that is empty over it

from.description: Only gaps starting at or after this time (seconds)

to.description: Only gaps ending at or before this time (seconds)

track.description: Track index

name: set_snap
description: When: Turn magnetic snapping on or off. Editor snap-to-clips/beats/bookmarks. Not undoable.

name: select_clips
description: When: Select several clips. Replace the selection with the given clips (UUIDs). Linked A/V partners are included.

name: set_transform
description: When: Position, size, rotate, fade a clip. Set canvas transform. Anchor model: positionX/positionY is where the clip's anchor lands on the canvas (project px, 0,0 = top-left; default the canvas centre, which is the clip's centre while the anchor is unset); scaleX/scaleY (or `scale` for both) resize the clip about its anchor, 1 = its fit size (frameW x frameH, read-only in the reply), so scaling never moves positionX/Y; rotation turns about the anchor. The reply's `box` {x,y,w,h} is the derived, unrotated on-canvas rect and cannot be written. 3D follows After Effects: x right, y down, z AWAY from the viewer (right-handed), and rotations pivot on the anchor point. Omitted fields are left unchanged. IMPORTANT: if the property is already animated (2+ keys), or autoKey is on, the write creates/updates a keyframe at the CURRENT PLAYHEAD (or at `at`, timeline seconds) instead of setting a constant value; that time must be inside the clip, else bad_args and nothing is written. A property with 0 or 1 key just takes the value. Use set_property_keyframes_enabled(false) or remove the keys for an unconditional value. Fails bad_args on audio clips and when no transform field is supplied.

anchorX.description: Anchor X in frame pixels (unscaled, from the frame's left edge): the pivot for scale and rotation, and the point positionX/Y places. Unset = the frame centre

anchorY.description: Anchor Y in frame pixels from the frame's top edge. Unset = the frame centre

anchorZ.description: Anchor point Z in pixels out of the clip's plane (+ away from the viewer; default 0)

at.description: Timeline seconds for the keyframe when the write keys (default: playhead); must be inside the clip

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

depth_occlude.description: Occlude by depth: this 3D layer hides and is hidden by other depth-occluding 3D layers (model and procedural clips) by z instead of track order. Needs a 3D layer with blend mode Normal; set it on every clip that should sort

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

layer3d.description: Make the clip a 3D layer (true) or flat (false). Writing any of the 3D fields below turns it on; false resets them to 0 and the default perspective

perspective.description: Eye distance from the canvas centre in pixels; smaller = stronger perspective. The default follows the project height (a 50 mm lens on a 36 mm film back: 2250 for a 1080 px canvas)

positionX.description: Canvas x in pixels where the clip's anchor lands (default: canvas centre)

positionY.description: Canvas y in pixels where the clip's anchor lands (default: canvas centre)

rotationX.description: Rotation about X in degrees (right-handed; + tips the top edge toward the viewer)

rotationY.description: Rotation about Y in degrees (right-handed; + swings the right edge toward the viewer)

scale.description: Uniform scale: sets scaleX and scaleY to this value; an explicit scaleX/scaleY wins

scaleX.description: Horizontal scale factor, 1 = fit size (not source resolution); scales about the anchor

scaleY.description: Vertical scale factor, 1 = fit size; scales about the anchor

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

z.description: Position Z in pixels; + away from the viewer, - toward it (After Effects' convention)

name: reset_transform
description: When: Reset a clip's position, size and rotation. Reset position (canvas centre), scale (1), rotation, 3D rotation/position Z/anchor/perspective (and the 3D layer switch), opacity, and flips to defaults. Video, image and vector clips return to their own shape fitted and centred on the canvas; other clips fill the canvas.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

description: When: Tune playback and cache settings. Change the global settings get_performance reports; only supplied keys change. They are the user's own settings, kept across sessions: change them for a round, then pass the reply's previous back to restore them. frame_cache_mib caps the decoded frame cache (0 = automatic, an eighth of RAM (a sixteenth on Android), at least 128; else 128–8192); clear_cache frees what's cached now. preview_quality auto|full|half|quarter|eighth. read_ahead_ms (0–5000) is how much each clip decodes ahead during playback. reset:true first puts the Performance page back to its defaults (not preview_quality or decode_mode). Out-of-range values are refused, and nothing changes. Not undoable. Returns get_performance's reply plus previous:{key: old value} for each key that changed.

The project and undo history are untouched. Returns {before, after}, each {frame_cache, decoders} as in memory_stats. Not undoable.

name: set_keyframes
description: When: Write many keys at once (bulk path, smooth). Write many keys on one or more properties in ONE call and one undo step; use it instead of a set_keyframe per key for camera paths and other dense animation. `keys` maps each prop to an array of [seconds, value] pairs ({at, value} objects work too); times are timeline seconds, clamped to the clip like set_keyframe. A key at an existing time overwrites its value. `replace:true` first clears each listed prop's existing keys. `interpolation` is applied to every key of each listed prop afterwards: linear, hold, ease, or smooth (Catmull-Rom auto tangents from neighbouring keys, written as bezier handles, so velocity is continuous across keys; dense linear keys look jerky, ease stops at every key). Omit it to leave the tangents alone. Props are validated like set_keyframe; one bad prop fails bad_args and nothing is written. Never writes the other axis of positionX/positionY. Returns {written:{prop:count}}.

name: add_model3d
description: When: Place a 3D model (.glb) or Gaussian splat. Add a glTF binary, or a Gaussian splat scene (.sog, a 3DGS .ply, a .zip or folder bundle holding meta.json/lod-meta.json, or that meta.json), as a model clip on a graphic track, creating one when needed. A model clip is a 3D layer like any other: its box (positionX/positionY and scaleX/scaleY on its frame) is the front face of the model's bounding box, z pushes it in depth (+ away from the viewer), rotationX/rotationY/rotation turn it about the clip's anchor (intrinsic, X then Y then the in-plane spin, the same as a tilted clip; the world is right-handed, y down, z away), and perspective is the eye it is seen through when there is no scene camera — set them with set_transform or set_keyframe like any clip. It occludes and is occluded by other 3D layers when "Occlude by depth" is on in the editor. It starts centred with its largest extent half the canvas height. scale/depth/rotX/rotY/rotZ are older shorthands still accepted: scale resizes the box about its centre to that fraction of canvas height, depth sets the perspective, rotX/rotY/rotZ set the rotations about the model's glTF axes (+y up, +z toward the viewer; written as rotationX = rotX, rotationY = -rotY, rotation = -rotZ). modelScale (default 1) resizes the model about the anchor and modelScaleZ (default 1) multiplies its depth, which is otherwise the geometric mean of the box's width and height scales. It is lit by ambient plus up to four point or spot lights (lights), placed like 3D Relight's across the clip's rect and near or far of the model's centre; they follow the clip's position and size but not its rotation. Their numbers are keyframable as model3d.ambient, model3d.modelScale, model3d.modelScaleZ and model3d.light<n>_<x|y|z|intensity|radius|cone|aimX|aimY>. A light's z is in clip heights, + away from the viewer, like the world's. An animated file plays its first animation at its own length unless duration is given; loop decides what happens past the end. Returns {id, track, index, animations:[{name, durationSec}], vertexCount, warning?, model3d:{…}}. A splat has no animations or lights (those options have no effect) and reports splatCount instead of vertexCount.

BLOCKS until done (a few seconds for a long range) and returns bpm, confidence, beatsPerBar, firstDownbeat, beats (absolute timeline seconds) and onsets [{at, s}] where s is 0..1 strength. duration must be at least 4 seconds and at most 600. WARNING: bpm 0 means no trustworthy tempo was found — the beats array is then empty, but onsets are still valid and unit:"onset" works everywhere a grid is accepted. Re-running the same range returns the cached result with cached:true unless force is set. The result is transient: any edit that changes the mix drops it. Returns error conflict when the editor is already analysing. Long lists are trimmed to 2000 beats / 500 strongest onsets, flagged as truncated. Call set_beat_layers next to make these beats snap targets.

SIDE EFFECT, and the reason to call it: only visible layers become snap targets, so with grid:true every later place_clip, move_clip and move_to_track magnets to the nearest beat within 150 ms, and so do the user's own drags. Turn it off to place something at an exact time instead. Onsets are thinned against beats so a dense track still leaves un-snapped positions. Returns the resulting flags plus snapTargets and snapEnabled — snapping does nothing when snapEnabled is false.

Skips any beat within 150 ms of an existing bookmark, since stacked markers make the magnet ambiguous rather than stronger. Requires detect_beats first. Returns {added}.

Returns clips (all resulting ids in timeline order, including the original) and at (the times actually cut). One undo step however many cuts it makes. min_gap drops cuts that would leave a sliver.

Dense music always has some onset nearby, so read audio_sync's chance figures before trusting a match.

name: audio_sync
description: When: Check sound lands on the cuts. For each cut, the audio event that answers it. Cuts are the video-track clip boundaries inside the range, or pass at:[…] for explicit times (required in asset mode, which has no timeline). status: ok = an onset within tolerance_ms; near = within 100 ms; swell = a build-up peaking within 300 ms; peak = no onset, only a soft level peak within 150 ms (check it); off = only a strong onset within 250 ms; no_sound = nothing. offset_ms = sound minus picture (negative = sound early). stats carry hit rates next to chance_* — what random cue times would score at this event density — and accent_* for strong accents only (>= 6 dB over the bed, top 20%): on a dense mix read those, a plain hit rate means little when chance is high. no_sound lists the cuts with no hit. Same clip / asset / timeline modes as audio_measure; range capped at 600 s; at beyond 400 cues is trimmed (truncated:true). BLOCKS. Fix a miss by moving the sound clip by offset_ms.

name: audio_tag
description: When: Name the sounds and sections. What a range sounds like, from the audio.clap addon (and audio.ast for speech and music). sections: the range cut where the sound changes (3 s windows merged while neighbours stay alike, split at strong timbre or level changes), each with a label (genre, instruments, mood, 'also:' sources from AST, ambience, voice), the top two vocabulary tags per category (music_genre, music_mood, instruments, ambience, voice) with z, and speech / music / silence probabilities. events: the most important hits and swells of audio_events (limit of them; those at a cut first), each with sound (WHOOSH, RISER, HIT, KEY, UI, STEP, FOLEY, NOTE, DRUM, VOICE), label, the top 3 sound tags with z, exposed (>= 12 dB over its bed, so the tag is more reliable) and sounds_like (calibrated vocabulary terms with verdict strong|plausible|weak). Tags on music mixes are guesses; trust exposed hits and z >= 2.5 sections. Same clip / asset / timeline modes as audio_measure; range capped at 600 s. BLOCKS (about a second per tagged event and per 2 s of section; a minute of audio takes tens of seconds on CPU). Missing addons return addon_missing.

name: audio_find
description: When: Find a sound by name. Where in a range a described sound happens. term is one of the 322 vocabulary terms (sound, music and ambience descriptions such as "heavy rain", "a fast whoosh", "applause", "crisp hi-hats"), or words that all appear in one ("whoosh" picks the shortest such term); the reply's term is the one used. There is no free-text search: anything else returns error unknown_term with the closest vocabulary terms in closest. Sliding windows plus excerpts around the strongest hits are scored with the calibrated CLAP match. Returns moments:[{start,end,z,cosine,verdict,source:window|event}] best first, non-overlapping, in the scope's seconds (timeline seconds, or source seconds in asset mode). z >= 3 strong (right 98% of the time on a held-out set), 2.5 plausible, 2 weak, below 2 nothing in this range sounds like the term. Same clip / asset / timeline modes as audio_measure; range capped at 600 s. BLOCKS (up to ~90 model runs). Needs the audio.clap addon (addon_missing otherwise).

name: audio_rank
description: When: Rank media by a sound. Rank media-bin audio and video assets by how well their sound matches one vocabulary term (same terms as audio_find; unknown_term lists the closest). Each file is embedded from up to six 10 s windows spread over it. Returns results:[{asset,name,z,cosine,verdict,near_silent,sounds_most_like}] best first; near-silent files (peak under -60 dBFS) rank last with verdict no match. z >= 3 strong, 2.5 plausible, 2 weak. Pick a sound effect or a clip from the bin by what it sounds like. Files without an audio track are listed in skipped_no_audio. At most 100 assets per call. BLOCKS (roughly a second per asset). Needs the audio.clap addon.

Returns segments:[{start,end,kind}] with kind speech | music | speech+music | silence | other (sound that is neither), plus speech_seconds, music_seconds and silence_seconds. Music under speech reads as speech+music. A window counts as speech or music from probability 0.3. Use it to find where dialogue is before ducking music, or where nothing is said. Same clip / asset / timeline modes as audio_measure; range capped at 600 s. BLOCKS. Needs the audio.ast addon.

name: audio_sheet
description: When: See the soundtrack. One annotated image of the sound over a range, on a shared time axis: a frame after each cut, labelled hits and swells, a 30 Hz-16 kHz spectrogram (silence is black), the waveform, momentary and short-term loudness with the integrated level and gaps shaded yellow, beat ticks, and a marker per cut coloured by sync (green onset within tolerance, amber within 100 ms, blue swell, violet level peak only, red no hit) with dashed cut lines through every lane. Use it to judge a whole mix at a glance — where the sound dies, what clips, whether hits land on the cuts. Same clip / asset / timeline modes as audio_measure; range capped at 600 s (zoom with start+duration). BLOCKS. Returns a summary, the measure numbers, events, cuts, sync stats and items (as audio_measure / audio_sync) and an inline JPEG (long edge <= 1600 px); return:"path" writes the full-width PNG to this session's agent-image cache folder (deleted when Drift quits, or swept after a day if it crashed; import_media copies it into the project) and returns its path instead. Asset mode draws frames only for video files and only at the at times. With the audio.clap / audio.ast addons installed the sheet also gets a sections lane, sound names on the hits and a speech / music lane (tags:false skips that and its model time; the reply then carries sections, tagged_events and presence, or tags_missing naming the addons to install). image result cannot run inside apply unless return is path.

name: detect_scenes
description:
When: Find the shots in a clip. Scan a video clip for shot boundaries and rank each shot by how much is happening. ASYNC: returns {started:true} immediately — poll inspect({detail:true}).jobs.sceneDetect {active, progress, status} until active is false, then read the result with list_scenes or describe_clip. Returns {cached:true} instead when this clip and these settings were already scanned, in which case the result is ready at once.
Unlike detect_beats, the analysis does NOT go stale on edits: it describes the source file, is cached against that file's timestamp, and survives edits, undo and reload. Re-trimming the clip does change the scanned range, so that scans afresh.
with_objects needs the object-model addon; without it the op fails with a message naming what to install.

description:
When: Read shots; sort:score for a highlight reel. The shots found by detect_scenes, as {scenes:[{index, start, end, duration, timeline_start, timeline_end, motion, loudness, objects, score, labels}]}. start/end are seconds into the SOURCE file; timeline_start/timeline_end are the same moments on the timeline, already mapped through the clip's trim, speed and reverse — use those to seek or cut. score is 0..1 and combines motion, loudness and objects. thumb/timeline_thumb is each shot's representative frame.
Pass clip (or track+index) for any clip that has been scanned; without one it reads the last scanned clip. Fails not_found for a clip that was never scanned.

name: market_status
description: When: See what the marketplace offers before searching it. Whether this build has a marketplace and what it serves: {configured, offline, revision, features, sources:[{id, kind, label, mediaKind, searchable, canResolve, categories (with children), providers?, sorts?}]}. Sources are stock.<type> (video, photo, audio, music, greenscreen), drift-assets, sfx and community.<kind> (effect, transition, audio-effect, look, theme, effect-template). source:<id> returns that one source in full. layout:true adds pages:[{id, title, sections:[{id, type, title, source}]}] so a section can be searched by its "page/section" name. refresh:true re-reads the server's manifest first (waits up to 15 s).

name: market_search
description: When: Find stock media, Drift assets, sounds or community add-ons. List one source, or run a section's own binding with section:"page/section" (its sort, category and page size become defaults). Returns {source, items:[{id, title, kind, dur?, w?, h?, by?, tags, category?, thumb, preview?, variants:n, installed}], next_cursor?, has_more, quota?, warnings?}. Omit q for the featured listing. category, sort and period use the values market_status lists for the source; provider "*" asks every provider; filters is a map of filter id to value. more:true fetches the next page of the previous search of that source (earlier ids stay valid); cursor restarts from a returned next_cursor. type is an alias for source:"stock.<type>". Blocks until the service answers. A resolve-only source needs market_resolve. Errors rate_limited, app_too_old and quota_exceeded come back as {ok:false, error, detail}.

name: market_resolve

name: market_preview

Fetches the item's thumbnail (what:thumb) or preview (what:preview), caches it under the app cache and returns a downscaled JPEG as image content with meta {path, w, h, mime}. Video and audio previews return meta {path, mime, dur} only, no image. image:false returns just the meta. Not batchable in apply: call it directly.

name: market_install
description: When: Install a listing into the project or the app. Install an item: stock media, Drift assets and sounds land in the media bin; community items install as an effect, theme, look or template; face props go to the face-prop library. Stock items SPEND the provider's per-machine quota (see market_search quota). Not undoable. Without wait it returns {job} at once; with wait:<seconds> (max 600) it blocks and returns {ok, job, result} where result is {asset} | {prop} | {effect} | {theme} | {look} | {template}. A failed or cancelled install comes back {ok:false, error, detail, job}. variant is a variant id from market_item; dir (stock only) is an absolute folder to save into. place:{at, track, new_track} puts the asset on the timeline once installed (needs wait > 0 and a bin asset) and adds {clip, placed, requested, reason?}; the placement is one undo step. An item that is still installing fails conflict.
