name: assemble
description: When: Build a sequence from an edit decision list. Place takes from several assets back to back: edl [{asset, start, end}] in source seconds, in play order (best take of each beat, any source). Appends to the end of `track` (default: the usual track for the first asset) unless `at` is given; video brings its linked audio. One undo step; nothing is left behind on failure. Returns {clips:[{id, src_start, src_end, start, end}], track, end}.

at.description: Timeline seconds to start at (default: after the track's last clip)

declick.description: Audio ramp at each cut, seconds

asset.description: Asset id

padding.description: Seconds added to both ends of each range

track.description: Target track index

name: diarize
description: When: Who speaks when. Label speakers in an asset's (or clip's) whole source file with the local diarize-model addon. Async: returns {job_id}; the job result is {speakers, segments:[{start,end,speaker}]} in source seconds, and an existing transcript gets its words labelled S1, S2… (read with get_transcript). transcribe({diarize:true}) does both in one pass.

asset.description: Asset id (alternative to clip)

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

min_off.description: Bridge same-speaker gaps shorter than this (s)

threshold.description: Cosine distance cut; lower finds more speakers

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: procedural_authoring_guide
description: When: How to write a procedural 3D package. Read before create_procedural. Returns {guide} - the full authoring guide (docs/procedural.md): package layout and manifest, the Lua API, budgets, the shader contract with both camera modes (world mode + a keyframed Camera clip is the recommended way to animate the view; scene:camera is for special cases), the unit-space toWorld/toBlock pattern, and a complete worked example.

name: list_procedurals
description: When: See installed procedural packages. Returns {procedurals:[{id, name, description, category, user, shaders:[names], params:[{key, label, type, min, max, default}]}]}. user:true marks packages made with create_procedural.

name: create_procedural
description: When: Write a new procedural 3D package. Create a package from a manifest, main.lua and shader pairs. Before anything is installed it is parsed, main.lua is run at t=0 with default params and camera, and every shader pair is compiled on the GL thread; failures return bad_manifest, lua_error or shader_compile_failed with errors[], the Lua log and the driver log per shader, and leave nothing on disk. Returns {id, stats:{meshCount, vertexCount, instanceCount, triangleCount, elapsedMs}, log, shaders:{name:{ok, log}}, shaderCheck: ok|skipped, warnings?}. id is user.<slug> and works with add_procedural at once. Not undoable. Do not call scene:camera in main.lua unless the shot must be self-contained: leave the script in world mode and frame it with add_camera + set_keyframes (see the guide).

manifest.description: procedural.json body (displayName, description, category, parameters, maxVertices, maxInstances); id is set for you

name: update_procedural
description: When: Change a My Procedurals package. Replaces parts of an existing user package by id, keeping the id so clips already using it pick the change up. Omitted manifest and files stay as they are; files overwrites or adds, remove_files drops shader files. edits patches files in place with exact-string replacements, applied in order after files (so a small fix does not need the whole script resent): each old must match its file exactly once, else the call fails bad_args naming the file and edit index and nothing is written. Validated like create_procedural. Bundled and add-on packages are refused (not_user_procedural) - fork those with create_procedural. Not undoable.

edits.description: Exact-string replacements applied to the package's files, in order, after `files`

old.description: Exact text to replace; must occur exactly once in the file

files.description: Only the files to overwrite or add, e.g. {"main.lua": "..."}

name: get_procedural_source
description: When: Read a procedural package's code. Returns {id, user, uses, manifest, files:{name: text}} for any package, bundled ones too, to learn from or fork. uses (user packages only) is how many clips in the project use it.

name: delete_procedural
description: When: Remove a My Procedurals package. Delete a user package. Refuses with in_use when the project has clips of it unless force:true (those clips keep their data and render nothing). Not undoable.

force.description: Delete even if the project uses it

name: add_procedural
description: When: Place a procedural 3D clip. Add a clip of an installed package on a graphic track, creating one when needed. It is a 3D layer the size of the canvas; the whole scene is built by main.lua each frame, in project pixels (origin top-left, y down, +z away); frame it with a Camera clip (add_camera, set_keyframes with interpolation "smooth" on positionX/positionY/z and anchorX/Y/Z, camera_look_at aimAtTarget) rather than scene:camera in the script. Params start at the manifest defaults; params sets starting values, and set_keyframe on proc.<key> animates them later (one key holds a constant). Returns {id, track, index}.

params.description: Starting values by param key; unknown keys fail bad_args

track.description: Optional destination graphic track; omitted picks or creates one

name: evaluate_procedural
description: When: Run a package's Lua and report the scene. Runs main.lua on the spot (no rendering) and returns {cameraMode: world|own, cameraRead, stats:{meshCount, vertexCount, instanceCount, triangleCount, luaBytesPeak, elapsedMs}, bounds:{min, max}, meshes:[{shader, vertices, instances, uniforms}], lights, camera? (own mode), log (print output), errors}. Give id to try a package with default params plus params overrides, or clip to evaluate a placed clip as it renders at timeline second t (keyframes, seed and the covering Camera clip included; params overrides still apply). cameraMode is world when the Camera clip frames the scene (recommended) and own when the script called scene:camera. Without clip, t is the script's `time`. A script error returns ok:false lua_error with errors[]. Use it to check bounds and counts without exporting.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

height.description: Canvas height for id mode (default: project)

id.description: Package id (when not evaluating a clip)

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

t.description: Seconds: script time for id; timeline time for clip (default 0, or the clip start)

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

width.description: Canvas width for id mode (default: project)

name: tts_generate
description: When: Voiceover from text (billable). Speak `text` with an ElevenLabs or Fish Audio voice and import the MP3 into the bin (and onto the timeline with place). BILLABLE on the user's account. Needs a key and the user's consent (errors not_configured / consent_required tell you what to ask for). Async: returns {job_id}; the job result has {asset, clip?, duration, path}. Voice ids come from list_voices; omitted = the default set in Settings. provider "local" runs Chatterbox on this machine instead: free, no key, needs the tts-model addon (local_tts_status); voice is a list_local_voices id, language/exaggeration apply, and place defaults to off (bin only).

exaggeration.description: local only: expressiveness, default the last used (0.5 at first)

language.description: ElevenLabs: ISO language code to enforce. local: Chatterbox language code (local_tts_status), default the last used

model.description: Model id; omitted = Settings default (eleven_multilingual_v2 / s2.1-pro)

place.description: true = at the playhead on a free audio lane; or {at, track}

voice.description: Voice id (ElevenLabs voice_id / Fish reference_id / local list_local_voices id)

name: sfx_generate
description: When: Sound effect from a prompt (billable). ElevenLabs text-to-sound-effects: import the result into the bin (and onto the timeline with place). BILLABLE. Async: returns {job_id}; the job result has {asset, clip?, duration}.

place.description: true = at the playhead; or {at, track}

prompt_influence.description: How literally to follow the prompt

name: list_voices
description: When: Voices you can speak with. Voices on the user's ElevenLabs or Fish Audio account (and public ones they can use). Returns {voices:[{id, name, …}], next?, default_voice}; pass next back as page.

mine.description: Fish: only the user's own voices

name: cloud_provider_status
description: When: Which cloud services are ready. For elevenlabs and fish: {configured, key_source, consent, tts_model, default_voice, stt_model}. Keys are never returned.

name: local_tts_status
description: When: Is local TTS ready. Local Chatterbox voice model: {available, model_loaded, loading, running, addon_id, languages:[{code,label}], last_voice, last_language, last_exaggeration}. available false = install addon_id first. warm_up starts loading the model now (about a minute) so the next generation doesn't wait; it returns at once.

warm_up.description: Start loading the model if it isn't loaded

name: list_local_voices
description: When: Local voice library. Voices for tts_generate provider local and voiceover_from_subtitles: {voices:[{id, name, built_in, source}]}. The built-in voice has id "default".

name: add_voice
description: When: Clone a voice from a sample. Add a voice to the local library from 3-20 s of clean speech: a file (path, absolute) or a clip's source audio (clip; the clip's trimmed range unless in/out are given). in/out are seconds in the source file; a longer range keeps its first 20 s. Needs the tts-model addon. Async: returns {job_id}; the job result has {voice, name}.

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

in.description: Sample start, seconds in the source file

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

out.description: Sample end, seconds in the source file

path.description: Absolute path of an audio or video file (instead of clip)

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

name: rename_voice
description: When: Rename a local voice. Rename a cloned voice. The built-in voice can't be renamed.

name: remove_voice
description: When: Delete a local voice. Delete a cloned voice and its stored sample. The built-in voice can't be removed.

name: voiceover_from_subtitles
description: When: Speak a subtitle clip. Speak every caption of a subtitle clip with a local voice, each line placed at its cue time on new audio tracks (one undo step). Needs the tts-model addon. Async: returns {job_id}; the job result has {placed, longer} (longer = lines that ran past their caption).

clip.description: Clip UUID from inspect({clips:true}) — preferred, stable across edits. Required unless both track and index are given; with neither the op fails not_found (it does not fall back to the selection).

index.description: Clip index on that track if clip is omitted

language.description: Chatterbox language code (local_tts_status); omitted = the last used

track.description: Track index if clip is omitted (0 = top). Positional — shifts when tracks are added or reordered.

voice.description: list_local_voices id; omitted = the last used

name: get_teleprompter
description: When: Read the teleprompter script and its settings. Read the Teleprompter panel: {script, lines, chars, speed, font_size, overlay, follow_recording, playing, position}. script is saved with the project. speed (lines per second), font_size, overlay (the script shown over the preview) and follow_recording (scrolling starts, pauses and stops with audio recording) are the user's global settings. playing and position (lines scrolled) are the live scroll.

name: set_teleprompter
description: When: Put a script in the teleprompter for the user to read. Put a script in the Teleprompter panel for the user to read while recording a voice-over themselves, and set how it scrolls. Only supplied keys change. The script is saved with the project and, as in the panel, is not undoable: replacing a non-empty script that differs fails conflict unless replace:true, so read it with get_teleprompter first. A new script stops the scroll and starts from the top. speed, font_size, overlay and follow_recording are the user's global settings, kept across sessions. Returns the settings plus lines and chars (not the script).

follow_recording.description: Scrolling starts, pauses and stops with audio recording

overlay.description: Show the script over the preview

replace.description: Allow replacing a different, non-empty script (default false)

script.description: The whole script; "" clears it. Line breaks are kept (\r\n becomes \n)

speed.description: Scroll speed in lines per second (panel default 0.6)
